q: The sequence of events that involves several different phases and brings about growth and asexual reproduction is called the _____
e: The sequence of events that involves several different phases and brings about growth and asexual reproduction is called the cell cycle. The cell cycle is the ordered sequence of growth, DNA copy, and division. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. Meiosis is different: meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles.

q: Interphase is subdivided into which of the following stages?
e: Interphase is subdivided into G1, S, G2. S is the synthesis stage of interphase when DNA is copied. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA. Meiosis I, Meiosis II, Cytokinesis is not G1, S, G2.

q: DNA replication occurs during the _____ stage of interphase.
e: DNA replication occurs during the S stage of interphase. DNA replication happens in S phase. S is the synthesis stage of interphase when DNA is copied. G2 is different: g2 is the growth and check stage after DNA has been copied.

q: After DNA replication, each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called _____
e: After DNA replication, each chromosome consists of two identical DNA molecules called chromatids. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Nucleotides is different: nucleotides are the monomers of DNA and RNA.

q: The point where two sister chromatids are joined together is called the _____
e: The point where two sister chromatids are joined together is called the centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. Centrosome is not centromere.

q: During the G$_2$ stage of interphase, the cell prepares for division by replicating _____
e: During the G2 stage of interphase, the cell prepares for division by replicating organelles. Interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA. DNA is different: dNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides.

q: The phase of the cell cycle that involves active nuclear division is called _____
e: The phase of the cell cycle that involves active nuclear division is called mitosis. Mitosis divides the nucleus so two daughter nuclei get identical chromosomes. The cell cycle is growth plus nuclear and cytoplasmic division. Interphase is different: interphase is G1, S, and G2, when the cell grows and copies DNA.

q: Cytokinesis refers to the separation of the _____
e: Cytokinesis refers to the separation of the cytoplasm. Cytoplasm is the fluid and structures inside the cell membrane, around the nucleus. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells.

q: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by the formation of a _____
e: In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by the formation of a cleavage furrow. Animal cells pinch in a cleavage furrow during cytokinesis. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Spindle fiber is not cleavage furrow.

q: In plant cells, cytokinesis involves the formation of a _____
e: In plant cells, cytokinesis involves the formation of a cell plate. Plant cells build a cell plate to divide the cytoplasm. Cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells. Centrosome is not cell plate.

q: The first phase of mitosis is _____
e: The first phase of mitosis is prophase. In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle starts to form. Mitosis divides the nucleus so two daughter nuclei get identical chromosomes. Anaphase is different: in anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

q: During prophase of mitosis, the _____ breaks down and the nucleolus disappears.
e: During prophase of mitosis, the nuclear envelope breaks down and the nucleolus disappears. The nuclear envelope breaks down in prophase and reforms in telophase. The nucleolus vanishes in prophase and returns in telophase. Cell membrane is not nuclear envelope.

q: Radial arrays of microtubules around each centriole are called _____
e: Radial arrays of microtubules around each centriole are called asters. Asters are microtubule arrays around the poles in animal mitosis. Kinetochores is not asters.

q: During metaphase of mitosis, chromosomes line up along the _____
e: During metaphase of mitosis, chromosomes line up along the metaphase plate. The metaphase plate is the equator where chromosomes align. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Cleavage furrow is different: animal cells pinch in a cleavage furrow during cytokinesis.

q: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its _____
e: Each chromatid becomes attached to the spindle by its centromere. The centromere is where sister chromatids are held and where spindle fibres attach. Sister chromatids stay attached at the centromere. Nucleolus is different: the nucleolus vanishes in prophase and returns in telophase.

q: In anaphase of mitosis, sister chromatids are pulled apart when the _____ divide.
e: In anaphase of mitosis, sister chromatids are pulled apart when the centromeres divide. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles. Spindles is not centromeres.

q: At the end of anaphase, the separated chromatids are now called _____
e: At the end of anaphase, the separated chromatids are now called chromosomes. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Sister chromatids are the two identical DNA copies joined at a centromere. Centrioles is not chromosomes.

q: During telophase, nuclear envelopes _____ around the two sets of chromosomes.
e: During telophase, nuclear envelopes reform around the two sets of chromosomes. Two nuclear envelopes form in telophase. Chromosomes carry genes; humans have 46 in diploid cells. Duplicate is not reform.

q: The result of mitosis and cytokinesis is two _____ daughter cells.
e: The result of mitosis and cytokinesis is two genetically identical daughter cells. Mitosis makes genetically identical body cells for growth and repair. Mitosis plus cytokinesis yields two genetically identical daughter cells. Genetically different is not genetically identical.

q: Meiosis occurs only in the _____
e: Meiosis occurs only in the sex organs. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Somatic cells is not sex organs.

q: Meiosis is also known as _____ division.
e: Meiosis is also known as reduction division. Chromosome number is reduced in meiosis I, not in mitosis. Equational is not reduction.

q: In animals, the formation of sperm is called _____
e: In animals, the formation of sperm is called spermatogenesis. Spermatogenesis is meiosis that produces sperm. Oogenesis is different: oogenesis is meiosis that produces eggs.

q: In flowering plants, meiosis produces microspores and megaspores that develop into _____
e: In flowering plants, meiosis produces microspores and megaspores that develop into gametes. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms. Zygotes is not gametes.

q: Meiosis involves _____ nuclear divisions.
e: Meiosis involves two nuclear divisions. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Three is different: dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts.

q: The pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I is called _____
e: The pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I is called synapsis. Synapsis is pairing of homologous chromosomes in meiosis I. Homologous chromosomes pair in meiosis; they carry the same genes but may have different alleles. Segregation is different: segregation is the splitting of allele pairs when gametes form.

q: Genetic variation is introduced during prophase I by _____
e: Genetic variation is introduced during prophase I by crossing over. Crossing over in prophase I swaps DNA between homologous chromosomes. Meiosis, crossing over, and random fertilisation generate genetic variation. Cytokinesis is different: cytokinesis splits the cytoplasm to finish making two cells.

q: During metaphase I of meiosis, _____ line up on the metaphase plate.
e: During metaphase I of meiosis, pairs of homologous chromosomes line up on the metaphase plate. Independent assortment concerns different pairs of homologous chromosomes. Homologous chromosomes pair in meiosis; they carry the same genes but may have different alleles. Sister chromatids is not pairs of homologous chromosomes.

q: In anaphase I of meiosis, the _____ do not divide.
e: In anaphase I of meiosis, the centromeres do not divide. In anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Nuclear envelopes is different: two nuclear envelopes form in telophase.

q: At the end of meiosis I, each daughter cell is _____
e: At the end of meiosis I, each daughter cell is haploid. Haploid cells have one set of chromosomes, as in gametes. Meiosis is reduction division that makes haploid gametes and shuffles alleles. Tetraploid is not haploid.

q: No _____ occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II.
e: No chromosome replication occurs between meiosis I and meiosis II. A chromosome is a DNA molecule with proteins, visible when condensed. Meiosis halves the chromosome number for gametes. Spindle formation is not chromosome replication.
